Software is only one aspect of archiving, the other important one is the hardware. Hard drives fail, therefore a robust backup strategy is a triple back-up in two separate physical locations, so data mirrored on two separate disks, then over over the network to a third remote storage location which you can either rent or set up yourself.

Some more concepts:
- Network attached storage (NAS), useful software for setting it up: FreeNAS
- Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) and the various RAID-levels, either improve performance (by striping) or help prevent data loss when a disk dies (by mirroring). - The lifespan of storage mediums:
SSDs and other flash storage can lose data after being turned off for too long (approx. 2+ years).
Hard drives often die within the first three years, but if they get past that will usually last longer and have a max. lifespan of 20-60 years, when the magnetic storage part of the firmware fades, data on HDDs is vulnerable to magnetic interference.
Magnetic Tape last longer, r/w is slower.
M-disks (kind of like a CD) are supposed to hold data for a century or two or even longer, if undamaged
